_default: I try it on the door. The door has seen burglars with better ideas.
It's a door. It wants a key or a code, not whatever that is.
I hold it against the door. The door stays shut. Doors are like that.
ledger: I press the Ledger against the door. It's a hardware wallet, not a hardware key. ...Close, though.
keycard: I look for a card reader on the front door. There isn't one. Adrian's front door is old-fashioned. Rude.
golden_token: I look for a coin slot in the front door. Nope. Shame. I'd pay to get in.
fence_plank: I could pry the door open with the plank. That's the breaking part. I'd rather skip to the entering.
note_half_a: Half a code opens half a door. Doors don't work like that.
note_half_b: Two digits. The door wants four. I'm exactly halfway to a door.

LOOK.text: A solid wooden door with a keypad. The display shows 4 empty digits waiting for a code.

then.text: I have the code, but I need to USE it on the keypad. Maybe I should try the code note with the door.

else.text: Locked. The keypad blinks red. I need a 4-digit code.

then.text: The door won't budge without the code. I should USE the code note on the keypad.

else.text: Locked tight. There's a keypad next to it. I need a code.

PICK.text: I can't pick up a door.

PUSH.text: I push the door. It's locked, not stuck.

PULL.text: I pull the handle. Still locked. The keypad judges me.

GIVE.text: I'm not giving anything to a door.

fence_plank: I could knock the note loose with the plank. And the bulb. And my eyebrows. There's a switch, Dex.
note_half_b: I hold the other half up to the light. Still ..14. The light doesn't fill in the rest.

then.text: Just a lamp now. Off, for the first time in three weeks. It looks relieved.
Just a lamp now. Off, for the first time in three weeks. It looks relieved.
Off now. The bracket's cooling down. Whatever's wedged back there is all mine.

else.text: Something's wedged behind the bracket. The bulb's been on for three weeks. I'm not touching that.

then.text: It's off. It's been on for three weeks. Let it have this.

else.text: Click. The moths drift over to the side window. They'll find another light. Everyone does.

then.text: Nothing else behind the lamp. Just a bracket and three weeks of moth history.
Nothing else behind the lamp. Just a bracket and three weeks of moth history.
I reach behind the bracket. Still warm, not lethal. A torn scrap of paper.
'73..' and then: 'The other half is with the birds. They never sell.'

else.text: Hot. Hot hot hot.

TALK.text: The light flickers. Morse code for 'hello'?

then.text: Nothing else behind the lamp. Just a bracket and three weeks of moth history.
Nothing else behind the lamp. Just a bracket and three weeks of moth history.
I pry the bracket open. A torn scrap of paper falls into my hand. Half a note.
'73..' and then: 'The other half is with the birds. They never sell.'

else.text: Hot. Hot hot hot.

then.text: Already off. The moths have filed for relocation.

else.text: No shade to close. There's a switch, though. Switches I can do.

PUSH.text: I push the lamp. It swings and creaks back.

then.text: I wiggle the bracket. Something papery rustles behind it.

else.text: I grab the bracket. Ow. Hot. The bulb's been on for three weeks and it's proud of it.

GIVE.text: The moths don't want anything from me.

LOOK.text: Warm light inside. I can see monitor screens glowing — someone's been running code.

USE.text: I tap on the glass. No response.

OPEN.text: Sealed shut from inside. Keeps the private keys safe.

PUSH.text: I push on the glass. Fingerprints everywhere now.

PULL.text: I pull the window frame. Sealed tight.

LOOK.text: A small window glowing orange. Cozy inside... or maybe something's on fire.

USE.text: Can't reach it through the bushes.

TALK.text: The curtain moves... wind or someone watching?

PUSH.text: I push through the bushes toward the window. Ouch.

PULL.text: I can't reach it through these thorns.

GIVE.text: The curtain twitcher doesn't want visitors.

_default: I could throw it up the drainpipe. I'd miss, and then it'd be up there too.
Too short. Anything I poke up there has to be long.
I wave it at the chimney. The chimney doesn't wave back. Chimneys don't do that.
note_half_a: I'm not offering the magpies the other half. They'd want the set.

then.text: Brick chimney. The drainpipe's nest-free now. The magpies are drafting a complaint.

else.text: Magpies nesting in the drainpipe, way too high to reach. They steal anything shiny.

USE.text: I'm not Santa. I'll use the door.

TALK.text: My voice echoes: '...not your keys, not your coins...'

then.text: Firmly attached to the building. The nest wasn't. That's the difference.

else.text: Too high. I'd need something long.

OPEN.text: Open at the top. That's how chimneys work.

PUSH.text: I push the bricks. Still solid after all these years.

then.text: I pull on the drainpipe. No nest left to fall. Just rust.

else.text: I jump for the drainpipe. I miss by a lot. The magpies watch. I'd need something long.

mystery_envelope: I almost put the envelope back in the mailbox. No. Finders keepers. That's the law. Roughly.
code_note: I'm not mailing the door code to anyone. That's how codes get leaked.

then.text: A rusty mailbox. Empty now.

else.text: A rusty mailbox overflowing with letters. Electric bills, mostly.

USE.text: I open the mailbox flap. Junk mail and... something else?

TALK.text: The mailbox creaks. It's been waiting for someone to check it.

then.text: Nothing else in the mailbox. Just old bills.

else.text: I sift through the junk mail... wait. A sealed envelope marked 'CONFIDENTIAL — PATIENT ZERO'. This looks important.

then.text: Nothing else in the mailbox. Just old bills.

else.text: I swing open the mailbox flap. Junk mail cascades out... and a sealed envelope marked 'CONFIDENTIAL — PATIENT ZERO' slides into view.

CLOSE.text: I close the mailbox. The flap doesn't stay shut.

PUSH.text: I push the mailbox post. It wobbles — years of neglect.

PULL.text: I pull on the mailbox door. Rusty hinges protest.

GIVE.text: I'm not mailing anything right now.

then.text: Overgrown bushes in front of the house. Wait... someone spray-painted 'ZERO WAS HERE' on the wall behind them.

else.text: Overgrown bushes in front of the house.
Overgrown bushes in front of the house.

USE.text: I rummage through. Ouch! Thorns. Nothing useful.

PUSH.text: I push through the bushes. Thorns grab my jacket.

PULL.text: I pull branches aside. More branches behind them.

GIVE.text: The bushes don't want my problems.

ledger: I put the Ledger back under the mat. Then I take it out again. Nobody needs to know.

then.text: I slide the doormat aside. Underneath — a hidden trapdoor with the AdrianZERO logo etched into it. The receptionist wasn't kidding.
VIP ACCESS — Found the holder-only shortcut to the basement

else.text: I wipe my feet.

then.text: Nothing else under the mat.

else.text: Under the mat... Adrian's Ledger! Someone hid it here.

then.text: I lift the doormat again. The hidden trapdoor with the AdrianZERO logo — VIP access to the basement.

else.text: Nothing else under the mat.
I lift the doormat. Underneath: Adrian's hardware wallet. Hidden in the most obvious place possible.

then.text: I shove the mat aside. There it is — a hidden hatch, VIP access to the basement. Holders only.

else.text: I push the mat aside with my foot.

then.text: I yank the mat back. The trapdoor underneath is still there. VIP shortcut to the basement.

else.text: I pull the mat. Heavy for a doormat.

GIVE.text: Nobody gives things TO a doormat.

LOOK.text: Concrete path to the door. Cracks form blockchain diagrams.

USE.text: Walking on it. Left, right. Decentralized movement.

TALK.text: No response. Hardened by years of foot traffic.

PICK.text: A pebble. Could be useful... probably not.

PUSH.text: I push against the concrete. It pushes back. Newton wins.

LOOK.text: Wooden power pole. The original Layer 1 — electrical infrastructure.

USE.text: I'd rather not touch live power lines.

PUSH.text: I push the pole. It doesn't budge. 50 years of infrastructure.

PULL.text: I pull on a low cable. Bad idea. I let go immediately.

GIVE.text: The power company doesn't accept hand deliveries.

LOOK.text: Dense trees. Leaves rustle in the evening breeze.

USE.text: I lean against a tree. Nature's proof-of-stake.

TALK.text: They've been here longer than any blockchain. Wise validators.

PICK.text: A leaf. Already turning orange. Like my portfolio.

OPEN.text: Behind the trees: more trees. And darkness.

PUSH.text: I push against a tree trunk. It's been doing this longer than me.

PULL.text: I pull a low branch. It snaps back. Ow.

LOOK.text: Red-brown tiles. Solid like a well-written smart contract.

USE.text: Can't reach from here. Need a ladder.

TALK.text: A bird takes flight, startled. Sorry.

PUSH.text: I can't reach the roof from here.

PULL.text: I'm not pulling tiles off a roof.

GIVE.text: The pigeons up there don't want anything.

LOOK.text: Empty carport. Oil stains but no car. Someone left in a hurry.

TALK.text: Footsteps echo. Ghost of a Lambo.

OPEN.text: Already open. More suggestion than shelter.

PUSH.text: I push the carport beam. It wobbles slightly.

PULL.text: I pull on the roof edge. Dust falls.

GIVE.text: The ghost Lambo doesn't need fuel.

_default: The keypad wants numbers. That isn't numbers.
I mash it against the keypad. It doesn't even beep. That's how bad an idea it was.
Keypads take codes. Not objects. Not hope.
ledger: I hold the Ledger up to the keypad. 'Hardware key,' I explain. The keypad only speaks digits.
keycard: I swipe the card across the keypad. It's a keypad. It has no idea what a card is.
mystery_envelope: The code isn't in the envelope. Probably. And I'm not opening confidential mail on a doorstep.
note_half_a: Half a code opens half a door. Doors don't work like that.
note_half_b: I type 1, 4. The keypad waits for the rest. So do I. The rest is somewhere else.
fence_plank: I could whack the keypad with the plank. It would still want four digits. Just angrier.

LOOK.text: A numeric keypad with backlit buttons. The display reads '_ _ _ _'. Four digits stand between me and whatever Adrian's hiding.

then.text: I could type the code here... but the front door keypad is the one that matters.

else.text: I tap random buttons. *BZZZ* 'INVALID CODE.' Better find the real code first.

TALK.text: I lean in and whisper 'password123'. The keypad blinks red. It's not amused.

PICK.text: It's screwed into the doorframe. I'd need tools and questionable morals.

OPEN.text: I pry at the faceplate. A tiny sticker warns: 'TAMPERING TRIGGERS SILENT ALARM. And Adrian's disappointment.'

CLOSE.text: The keypad is always on. Always waiting. Like a limit order I forgot about.

PUSH.text: I press all the buttons at once. *BZZZ BZZZ BZZZ* That's not how keypads work.

PULL.text: I tug at the keypad. It's firmly mounted. Security by stubbornness.

GIVE.text: I'm not giving a keypad anything. It hasn't earned my trust.

LOOK.text: A blazing pink and orange sunset. Like watching a candlestick chart go parabolic across the entire sky.

USE.text: I try to screenshot the sunset. My phone camera does NOT do it justice. Some things can't be minted.

TALK.text: 'Hey sky, when moon?' The clouds drift silently. Even the atmosphere won't give me alpha.

PICK.text: I reach for the sunset. My arm isn't long enough. Story of my trading career.

OPEN.text: Can't open the sky. It's already the most permissionless thing in existence.

CLOSE.text: The sun is closing on its own. Give it twenty minutes.

PUSH.text: I push against the fading light. Physics remains unimpressed.

PULL.text: I try to pull the sunset back. Time only moves in one direction. Like my portfolio.

GIVE.text: The sky doesn't accept offerings. Not even gas fees.

_default: I lean it against the fence. The fence doesn't need help. It needs a plank back.
The fence takes nothing. It only gives. One plank, specifically.
I tap it on the fence. Wood says hello. Nothing else happens.
fence_plank: I try to put the plank back. It doesn't fit anymore. Some things you can't undo. I'm keeping it.

then.text: The fence, minus one plank. Adrian will notice. Eventually. Probably.

else.text: A weathered wooden fence. One plank hangs on by a single nail. It's basically asking.

USE.text: I lean on the fence. It creaks but holds. More reliable than most DeFi protocols.

TALK.text: 'Good fences make good neighbors.' The fence says nothing. It's a fence.

then.text: I've got my plank. I'm not taking the whole fence. I'm a detective, not a demolition crew.

else.text: One plank is barely hanging on. Picking won't do it. That needs a good pull.

OPEN.text: No gate here. Just fence all the way. Permissioned access only.

CLOSE.text: The fence is already doing its best impression of a closed position.

PUSH.text: I push the fence. It leans. One more push and Adrian's property value drops 3%.

then.text: One plank is enough. I'm a detective, not a demolition crew.

else.text: I pull a plank. It comes loose. Now there's an exploit in the perimeter. I'm the exploit.

GIVE.text: The fence doesn't want anything. It just wants to be left alone. Relatable.

LOOK.text: Four windows glow warmly on the second floor. Multiple monitor screens visible inside. Someone was running serious operations up there.

USE.text: Too high to reach from here. I'd need to get inside first.

TALK.text: 'Anyone trading up there?!' The glow of the screens is the only answer. The bots never sleep.

PICK.text: Can't reach the second floor. I'm not Spider-Man. I'm more of a rug-pull survivor.

OPEN.text: Way too high. I'd need a ladder or a very optimistic leverage position.

CLOSE.text: The curtains are already half-drawn. Privacy mode: on.

PUSH.text: I push against the wall below the windows. The house doesn't budge. Solid foundation.

PULL.text: I try to pull myself up toward the windows. Gravity says no. Hard no.

GIVE.text: I can't give anything to windows I can't reach. Story of every failed airdrop claim.

else.text: That trail climbs straight into the mountains. No idea where it leads, and I'm not hiking blind. My cardio is more bearish than my portfolio.

then.text: The nest's already down. Poking the chimney now would just be petty.
I poke the nest down. Twigs, a bottle cap, a gum wrapper. Nothing I still need.

else.text: I poke the nest with the plank. It drops at my feet. Twigs, a bottle cap... and a scrap of paper wrapped in foil.
Magpies steal anything shiny. Finally, someone with my investment thesis.

script.text: I hold the note up to the keypad. 7... 3... 1... 4...
*BEEP* Green light! The front door clicks open.
I punch in the code from the note: 7-3-1-4...

else.speaker: Narrator
else.text: Three weeks after Adrian, creator of ZERO, vanished, his wallet messaged Dex.
"Find Patient Zero. Bring them home. Everything in the lab is yours."
Everything? I'm already at the door.
